full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim J:- This Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 11th and 12th day of August, 2008 passed by the High Court Division in EA. No. 462 of 1999 The facts involved in the case, in short, are that the suit property as described in the plaint was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 629 which consists of C.S. Plot No. 650 and 651 of which Bonobihari was the owner of 78/15 decimals which has been described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint. Bonobihari left behind five sons, namely, Rashik Lal Ghosh, Keshob La! Ghosh, Jadu Lal Ghosh, Madhusudhan Ghosh and Sadhu Lal Ghosh and thus, they owned the 'Ka' schedule land by inheritance and had been possessing the same in ejmali. They lived in the undivided joined family. While owning and possessing all the properties in the joint family they acquired .10,0 decimals of land as described in schedule `Kha' to the plaint by way of purchase vide registered kabalas dated 27.09.1961 and 18.02.1961. The said two kabalas were registered in the name of Keshob Lal Ghosh on behalf of his five brothers and all of them used to own and possess the same in equal shares. The 'Ka' scheduled land was purchased by the income of all the above five brothers living in ejmali in the joined family. Rashik Lal Ghosh left behind only son Rango Lal Ghosh who then sold out .4-111-375 decimals out of 'Ka' and `Kha' schedule land to his uncle Madhusudhan and delivered up possession thereof to him. Madhusudhan acquired .4121375 decimals of land and .4375dceimals of land by way of purchase and inheritance out of the suit land. He then died leaving five sons namely, the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and defendant Nos. 14 and 15 and of whom, thus got share in the suit land to the extent of 123 decimals each. Sadhu Lal Ghosh died leaving one son, namely Shanti Ghosh-defendant No.11 who sold .41-1-12 decimals of land out of the suit land to defendant Nos.9 and 10 and the plaintiff Nos. 1-3 and each of the plaintiffs thus, got 11-112 decimals of land out of the suit land by way of purchase and inheritance. The plaintiffs acquired .524decimals of land jointly out of the suit land and they have been possessing the same in ejmali with other co-sharers. Jadhu Lal Ghosh left behind only son, namely, Kartick who sold some portion of his share in the suit land to Ghiridhari Ghosh son of Keshob Lal Ghosh, Kartick died leaving only son Dilip Ghosh who inherited the rest share of Kartick. Keshob Lal died leaving Nos. 5-10 as heirs. The aforesaid Ghiridhari died leaving defendant No. 4 as wife and defendant Nos. 1, 3 as sons. The plaintiffs possess lesser quantum of land then their legitimate share in the suit land. They asked the defendant Nos. 1-5 to effect amicable partition of the suit land but they refused to comply with on 05.09.1992 by disclosing that defendant No. 16 Momitazuddin Ahmed, Aftabuddin Ahmed and Waizuddin Akram took signatures of Keshob Lal and his sons, namely Ghiridhari and Trinath on unwritten blank stamp and cartridge papers during the liberation war of Bangladesh in 1971 when Keshob Lal and his family members left this country for India. The sons of Keshob Lal Ghosh further disclosed that the above Momtazuddin and others took their signatures on the plea of protecting the suit properties and Keshob and others put their signatures on good faith on the advice of Momtazuddin and others fraudulently manufactured a bainapatra in respect of the 'Ka' scheduled land by ping those signed stamp and cartridge paper and filed Title Suit No. 36 of 1971 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka against Keshob Lal for, specific performance of contract and fraudulently obtained a decree which is illegal, inoperative and no binding upon the plaintiffs. Momtazuddin and others filed Title Execution Case No. 8 of 1991 for execution and registration of a safkabala in pursuance of the decree. Since the defendants refused to effect partition of the suit property and since they obtained the fraudulent decree in Title Suit No. 36 of 1971, the plaintiffs are entitled to get partition of the suit property with a declaration that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 36 of 1971 is illegal, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 2. The 'defendant Nos.16-21 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material allegation con-tending, interalia, that the plaintiffs have no cause of action in filing the suit and they have also no Jocus standi to file the suit and that the quit is also not maintainable as the plaintiffs: have no ownership and possession in the suit land. The defendants further contended that Bonobihari Ghosh was the original owner of the 'Ka' schedule property who left behind five sons who inherited the 'Ka' scheduled land with their successive heirs and thus, they are entitled to get partition in respect of the 'Ka' scheduled land to the plaintiff to which the defendants have no claim; that the `Kha' scheduled land to the plaintiff exclusively belonged to Keshob Lal Ghosh by way of purchase. Keshob Lal on 28.11.1969 sold out the `Kha' scheduled land to these defendants by executing a bainapatra with the due delivery of possession thereof. Keshob Lal Ghosh and others thereafter, having refused to execute and register a safkabala, the defendants filed Title Suit No. 36 of 1971 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for specific performance of con-tract in respect of the `Kha' scheduled land to the plaint which was legally decreed on contest on 31.08.1974 against which Keshob and others preferred appeal being Title Appeal No. 53 of 1975 before the High Court Division which was dismissed on contest. Thereafter, Keshob and others filed petition for leave to appeal before the Appellate Division which was also dismissed on contest. The defendants, there-after, filed Title Execution Case No. 8 of 1991 for execution of the decree passed in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 36 of 19781 and the said Execution Case is still pending. The defendant Nos. 1-10 contested the case contending that in-spite of the fact they got the suit filed by the plaintiffs out of malafide intention and they got no ownership and possession in the `Kha' scheduled land for over 24 years since after Keshob Lal and others sold the same vide the bainapatra executed in 1969. In S.A. Khatian the suit land in `Kha.' scheduled had been duly recorded in the name of Keshob Lal which was never challenged by the plaintiffs. It is expressly averred in the kabala that Keshob purchased the said property by his own personal wealth and means and the same was never purchased by the wealth and money of the undivided joint family that the plaintiffs have no locus standi to challenge the decree passed in Title Suit No. 36 of 1971 and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.
